stories.title: Effects of real-time and potential traffic congestion on network throughput
stories.description: To reduce traffic congestion and improve network throughput, this study focuses on the dynamic routing process by constructing a unified path-cost function that integrates both a real-time traffic congestion index (derived from instantaneous node queue lengths) and a potential traffic congestion index (estimated from the expected number of future paths traversing each node based on active routing decisions). Through extensive simulations on Barabási–Albert scale-free network and Erdös–Rényi random network, we systematically investigate how these two types of congestion information affect network throughput. The results reveal that real-time traffic congestion is more significant than potential traffic congestion in improving network throughput. By comparison with five routing algorithms, it is found that the routing strategy considering both real-time and potential traffic congestion are more efficient. The main contribution of this work is to reveal the impacts of real-time and potential congestion on network throughput, clearly establishing their primary-secondary relationship in throughput control, and providing empirical guidelines and parameter-tuning recommendations for hybrid routing designs that combine immediate responsiveness with predictive awareness.

stories.title: Operational feasibility of drone based BVLOS transport for temperature sensitive oncosurgical specimens from a secondary to tertiary hospital corridor in India
stories.description: Timely intraoperative pathological diagnostics, such as frozen section analysis, are critical for optimizing oncosurgical outcomes. Peripheral secondary care hospitals often lack the necessary infrastructure, causing delays and hindering effective surgical decision-making. Traditional road-based specimen transport faces challenges like prolonged transit times and inadequate temperature maintenance. Drones, or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), offer a potential solution for rapid and reliable transport. The study was conducted from January to April 2024 between Dr. T.M.A. Pai Rotary Hospital in Karkala and Kasturba Medical College in Manipal. Hybrid VTOL drones (AD350 model) completed 21 BVLOS missions along a pre-approved 25.4 km semi-urban corridor. The Project Domain Framework and extended TELOSS analysis evaluated three transport alternatives. Specimens remained within the required 2–8 °C range through triple packaging, gel-ice packs, and continuous temperature logging. Primary measures included flight success rates, transit times, temperature control, and regulatory compliance. All 21 BVLOS flights succeeded, reducing transport time from an estimated 50–60 min by road to 21 min by drone, an estimated 65–70% improvement. Every specimen maintained stable temperatures between 2 and 8 °C. Seven patients contributed eight intraoperative oncosurgical specimens, as one patient provided two specimens during the same operative session. All specimens processed through standard pathology protocols demonstrated complete histo-morphological integrity. Frozen section reports were delivered in an average of 15.3 min. Specimens were collected from patients undergoing surgery for suspected oncological conditions; histopathological evaluation confirmed malignancy in three of eight specimens, with the remaining five specimens found to be non-malignant. TELOSS analysis showed drone transport for crucial specimens achieved the highest scores across all feasibility domains. BVLOS drone operations proved technically feasible, regulatory compliant, and operationally viable for transporting temperature-sensitive medical specimens across semi-urban healthcare corridors. The approach offers a scalable solution for India’s tiered healthcare system.
